newsitem.title: USA: Florida high court blocks assisted suicide.
newsitem.headline: Florida high court blocks assisted suicide.

text.p: A terminally ill Florida man's request to kill himself with his doctor's help was on hold indefinitely Wednesday after the Florida Supreme Court re-instituted a stay on a lower court decision giving him permission to take his life.

Florida's highest court agreed late Tuesday to hear the state's appeal in the case of Charles Hall, a 35-year-old Citrus County man who contracted AIDS from a blood transfusion more than 15 years ago.
In a two-page, unsigned decision, the state Supreme Court justices scheduled oral arguments for May 9 and re-imposed a stay issued immediately after a lower court ruled in Hall's favour.

Hall, who suffers a host of AIDS-related maladies including severe infections, partial blindness and repeated bouts of pneumonia, is requesting that he be given the right to kill himself with the help of his physician, Dr. Cecil McIver of Jupiter, Fla.

A state circuit court judge in Palm Beach County granted Hall's request Jan. 31, throwing out a 129-year-old state law prohibiting assisted suicide. The case was immediately appealed by state attorneys and a stay was issued.

An appellate court lifted the stay Feb. 6 but requested the state Supreme Court to hear the case. Hall's case has received national attention as the country wrangles with the issue of physician-assisted suicide.
In January, the U.S. Supreme Court heard arguments and will decide whether state laws in Washington and New York approving physician-assisted suicide are constitutional.
Oregon is the only U.S. state where physician-assisted suicide is legal. The law, passed by Oregon voters in 1994, has been challenged and has yet to take effect.

In contrast, 35 U.S states have laws expressly forbidding assisted suicide. Nine states have common law prohibitions. In five states the laws are unclear. Hall's attorney, Robert Rivas of Boca Raton, could not immediately be reached for comment.
